title: Chicken Adobo
subtitle: Filipino braised chicken in vinegar, soy, and bay leaves
excerpt: Chicken pieces braised in a simple sauce of white vinegar, soy sauce, garlic, and bay leaves until the liquid reduces to a sticky, tangy glaze. The national dish of the Philippines.

recipe.sourceNotes: Chicken adobo is the national dish of the Philippines and one of the most widely eaten dishes in Filipino cooking. The word adobo refers both to a cooking method and a marinade derived from the Spanish word adobar (to marinate). Filipino adobo is distinct from Mexican or Spanish adobo: it is a braise in vinegar and soy sauce rather than a chilli-based preparation. The combination of vinegar and salt has a preservative effect, which allowed the dish to be kept for several days without refrigeration, an important practical quality in the Philippine climate. Each family has its own version, varying the ratio of vinegar to soy, the type of vinegar, and the addition of coconut milk, turmeric, or sugar.

recipeTools.notes: Wide enough to hold all the chicken in a single layer.

content.text: The key to adobo is reducing the sauce until it clings to the chicken in a sticky, concentrated glaze. The initial braise cooks the chicken through; the final stage removes the lid and lets the liquid evaporate until the sauce is thick and the chicken is slightly caramelised. Watch carefully at this stage: the soy sugars can burn quickly. Use bone-in thighs for the best flavour: they stand up to the long braise better than breast meat.

items.preparation: optional, to balance if very sharp

content.text: Combine the vinegar, soy sauce, garlic, bay leaves, peppercorns, and water in a bowl. Add the chicken and marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours in the fridge.

Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Remove the chicken from the marinade (reserving the marinade) and brown skin-side down for 4 to 5 minutes until golden. Flip and cook 2 minutes more. Pour the marinade over the chicken. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook on low heat for 25 minutes.

Remove the lid. Increase the heat to medium and cook for a further 15 to 20 minutes, turning the chicken occasionally, until the sauce has reduced to a thick, sticky glaze that coats the chicken. Taste: add a teaspoon of sugar if it is very sharp. Serve with steamed white rice.
